newsitem.title: UK: W. AFRICA 130KT, UKC 80KT RATES UP, SHIPS SCARCE.
newsitem.headline: W. AFRICA 130KT, UKC 80KT RATES UP, SHIPS SCARCE.

text.p: Chartering rates for 80,000 tonne tankers in the UK/Cont region and for 130,000 tonne vessels sailing west from West Africa were both firmer again on Wednesday amid a scarcity of vessels, brokers said.

Dealers said that Mobil's fixture of the 80,000 tonne Berge Hugin at a heady W125 were at the higher end of the day's range because of tight timing requirements but they added that Total's W115 paid for the 80,000 tonne Sidelia was at the lower end of the range.
"There is a lack of tonnage, it is as simple as that," one broker said. "The same goes for Suezmaxes from West Africa."
A rash of fresh 130,000 tonne fixtures from West Africa to the U.S. were concluded at around W92.5 to W95, a rise of over 10 points since last week.
Mideast/Japan rates for 250,000 tonne VLCCs were still firm, talked in the high W80s, but chartering activity was relatively muted.
Suezmaxes in the Mediterranean were slightly quieter although continued chartering to pick up Iraqi oil from Ceyhan was keeping rates at a firm W90-95.
Rates for other sizes of ships on other routes were little changed.
